accepted.label: String Encoding and Decoding in Python
accepted.description: Understanding that strings in Python 3 are sequences of Unicode characters, and how to encode strings to bytes using specified encodings (e.g., UTF-8) and decode bytes back to strings, handling potential encoding errors.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe the difference between a string and a bytes object.
Given a string and an encoding name, student can write code to encode and decode it correctly.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate provides a self-contained teachable concept on text encoding and decoding, fundamental for NLP text preprocessing.

accepted.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP) Definition
accepted.description: NLP is a branch of AI that enables machines to read, understand, and derive meaning from human languages, combining linguistics and computer science.
coverage_criteria: Define NLP and its two foundational fields: linguistics and computer science.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate defining NLP; no merge needed.

accepted.label: Everyday Applications of NLP
accepted.description: Common NLP applications include autocorrect for spelling and plagiarism checkers that scan for duplicate content.
coverage_criteria: List and describe two everyday NLP applications, such as autocorrect and plagiarism checking.
accepted.merge_rationale: Single candidate covering everyday NLP applications; no merge needed.

accepted.label: Text Preprocessing: Segmentation, Tokenization, and Stop Words
accepted.description: The initial NLP steps: breaking documents into sentences (segmentation), sentences into words (tokenization), and removing common stop words to focus on meaningful content.
coverage_criteria: Explain segmentation, tokenization, and the role of stop words in NLP preprocessing.
accepted.merge_rationale: These three candidates cover sequential preprocessing steps that are often taught together in introductory NLP; merging into one concept reduces fragmentation while preserving teachable granularity.

accepted.label: Word Normalization: Stemming and Lemmatization
accepted.description: Stemming reduces words to root forms by cutting suffixes (e.g., 'skipping' → 'skip'), while lemmatization uses dictionary-based analysis to find base forms (e.g., 'am', 'are', 'is' → 'be').
coverage_criteria: Define stemming and lemmatization, and contrast one with the other with examples.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both are word normalization techniques; merging them into one concept allows a clear comparison and avoids too much granularity.

accepted.label: Linguistic Annotation: POS Tagging and Named Entity Recognition
accepted.description: POS tagging labels words with grammatical categories (noun, verb, etc.), while Named Entity Recognition identifies names, locations, and organizations in text.
coverage_criteria: Explain what POS tagging and Named Entity Recognition are, giving examples of each.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both are annotation tasks applied to text after preprocessing; merging them provides a unified concept of linguistic annotation.

accepted.label: Machine Learning in NLP
accepted.description: After preprocessing, ML algorithms like Naive Bayes can be applied to tasks such as sentiment analysis, learning patterns from labeled data.
coverage_criteria: Describe the role of machine learning in NLP, giving Naive Bayes as an example.
